name: physical-constants

description.en: 35 fundamental physical constants in 70 cards: the seven exact defining constants of the SI, constants derived exactly from them, and measured constants of electromagnetism, atomic physics and gravitation, including the Planck units. For each constant one card asks for its standard symbol and one for its value (with unit where it has one). Values are exact where the SI makes them exact; otherwise they are the CODATA 2022 recommended values rounded to 5 significant figures and marked ≈. Values use a decimal point, as in CODATA's tables, and digits grouped in threes; the Swedish notes follow Swedish practice with a decimal comma. Compiled from the CODATA 2022 report (arXiv), the BIPM SI Brochure, Swedac's regulations on units (STAFS 2009:26) and Wikidata, and checked against NIST's CODATA tables.
description.sv: 35 fundamentala fysikaliska konstanter i 70 kort: SI:s sju exakta definierande konstanter, konstanter som exakt härleds ur dem och uppmätta konstanter inom elektromagnetism, atomfysik och gravitation, bland dem Planckenheterna. För varje konstant frågar ett kort efter dess vedertagna beteckning och ett efter dess värde (med enhet där den har en). Värdena är exakta där SI gör dem exakta; i övriga fall är de CODATA:s rekommenderade värden från 2022, avrundade till 5 värdesiffror och markerade med ≈. Värdena skrivs med decimalpunkt, som i CODATA:s tabeller, och siffrorna grupperade tre och tre; de svenska anteckningarna följer svensk skrivsed med decimalkomma. Sammanställd ur CODATA:s rapport från 2022 (arXiv), BIPM:s SI-broschyr, Swedacs föreskrifter om måttenheter (STAFS 2009:26) och Wikidata, och kontrollerad mot NIST:s CODATA-tabeller.

method: Who did the work. Anton Wiklund compiled this deck with the help of AI agents (Claude, by Anthropic), which did the research, drafting and cross-checking at his direction. The cards were checked by machine (live Wikidata and the app's SHACL and DCAT-AP validators) and in independent review rounds by further Claude agents, each logged under Quality control with its findings and how they were resolved. Anton Wiklund reviews every deck in full before it is released.

Which CODATA release. Downloaded NIST's constants home page and version history (Queries) on 2026-10-04. The version history says the 2022 CODATA values are "the latest CODATA values available" (Version 9.0, 9 May 2024), and the home page announces the 2026 adjustment, for which data must be published before 31 December 2026. So the 2022 values (published in Reviews of Modern Physics on 30 April 2025) are the current recommended values on 2026-10-04.

Licences. The brief named NIST's CODATA pages as a public-domain content source. NIST's licensing statement says the Secretary of Commerce may secure copyright in Standard Reference Data, and the constants database is NIST Standard Reference Database 121, so it was used for verification only. The CODATA 2022 report itself is on arXiv (2409.03787v1) under CC BY 4.0 and was used as the content source for values, symbols and English names; the BIPM SI Brochure (CC BY 4.0) for the seven defining constants. The published article (APS) carries no open licence and was used only to check that the preprint's table matches it. This makes the deck CC BY 4.0 (see Licensing).

Values. Extracted the text of the arXiv PDF with pypdf and read Table XXXIII (PDF pp. 51–55); downloaded NIST's complete ASCII listing (allascii.txt). values.py parses allascii.txt; crosscheck.py found the full digits of 33 of the 35 values in both the arXiv text and the published article's text; the two missing ones, the caesium frequency and the luminous efficacy Kcd, are not in CODATA's tables (a hit for 683 was only part of another number, the neutron-electron mass ratio 1838.683 662 00, so it does not count). The seven defining constants (exact) come from BIPM Table 1 and STAFS 2009:26 bilaga 1.1, which agree with each other and with NIST digit for digit; five of them are also in arXiv Table XXXIII.

Rounding convention. Exact values of the seven defining constants are given in full. All other values are rounded to 5 significant figures (round half to even, computed with Python's decimal module from NIST's full digits) and marked with ≈: both the measured constants (whose standard uncertainty is far below the fifth significant figure; the largest relative uncertainty, that of G, is 2.2 × 10⁻⁵) and the constants that are exact since 2019 but have long or endless decimal expansions (ħ, R, F, σ, b, c₁, c₂; CODATA truncates them with "..."; R and F terminate, after 15 and 18 significant digits, the other five never end). Each value card's note says which kind it is. Number format follows the SI Brochure (Section 5.4.4): digits in groups of three separated by a space on both sides of the decimal marker, but no space when there are only four digits; the decimal marker is the point, as in the English SI Brochure and CODATA, since the value is written once for all languages (tag zxx). Powers of ten and unit exponents use Unicode superscripts (× 10⁻³⁴, m s⁻¹); units are written as in CODATA's tables with a space between unit symbols (J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹), except that the Planck constant's unit is J s as in the SI Brochure and STAFS (CODATA 2022 writes J Hz⁻¹; the note says so).

Symbols. Symbols follow CODATA Table XXXIII and BIPM Table 1, in Unicode: ħ (U+0127), μ (U+03BC), ε (U+03B5), Δ (U+0394), subscript digits (μ₀, ε₀, Z₀, a₀, c₁, c₂) and subscript letters where Unicode has them (mₑ, mₚ, mₙ, mᵤ, rₑ, μₑ). Unicode has no subscript capital letters and no subscript c, d or C, nor a subscript ∞, so ΔνCs, NA, Kcd, λC, μB, μN, lP, mP, tP, TP and R∞ are written with the subscript on the line, and the card's note says which part is the subscript (e.g. "N with subscript A"). The Boltzmann constant's symbol is k, as in CODATA and BIPM Table 1; its note says it is also written kB (as in the SI Brochure's Appendix 1 and Swedish Wikipedia).

Selection. Started from the brief (about 35 constants: the seven defining constants plus well-known derived and measured constants) and CODATA Table XXXIII. Kept every constant whose English name is CODATA's and whose Swedish name could be confirmed in at least one Swedish source beyond our own translation (see step 9). One exception: the proton-electron mass ratio, whose Swedish name "kvoten mellan protonens och elektronens massor" is our own descriptive translation (Swedish Wikipedia full-text searches for it and for other phrasings found nothing, and Wikidata Q2912520 has no Swedish label); it was kept because the ratio itself is well attested in Swedish (Swedish Wikipedia, Proton and Elektron: "1836,15 gånger elektronens massa") and the name only describes it. The first and second radiation constants rest on a single Swedish attestation each (see Selection). See Selection for the list and what was left out.

English names: CODATA's names from arXiv Table XXXIII and NIST's listing, and BIPM's for the defining constants ("Hyperfine transition frequency of Cs-133" is NIST's name and a Wikidata alias; BIPM says "hyperfine transition frequency of Cs"). Two deliberate departures: "Electron Compton wavelength" (Wikidata's label) instead of CODATA's bare "Compton wavelength", because CODATA also lists Compton wavelengths of other particles; and the luminous efficacy is named in full ("... of monochromatic radiation of frequency 540 × 10¹² Hz") as in the BIPM text and Wikidata, because "luminous efficacy" alone is a general quantity, not a constant.

Swedish names. For the seven defining constants: STAFS 2009:26 bilaga 1.1, Swedish law's definitions of the base units (cesiumfrekvensen, ljusets hastighet i vakuum, Plancks konstant, elementarladdningen, Boltzmanns konstant, Avogadros konstant, ljusutbytet för monokromatisk strålning med frekvensen 540 × 10¹² Hz). For the others: the Swedish Wikidata label where one exists and matches Swedish usage (SPARQL queries under Queries), otherwise our own translation of the CODATA name. Every Swedish name was then checked against Swedish Wikipedia (article titles and leads fetched with the MediaWiki API, full-text search for names without an article, and the table in Fysikalisk konstant) and against Nationalencyklopedin's free article introductions (fetched by headword; ne_fetch.py under Queries). Each card's evidence quotes what those pages say. Names of quantities that are commonly used in the definite form in Swedish are given in the definite form, as NE and Swedish Wikipedia use them (gravitationskonstanten, Bohrradien, Plancklängden).

Card text. Front "<name>: symbol" / "<namn>: beteckning" (STAFS's and NE's word for a symbol) and "<name>: value" / "<namn>: värde"; back in no language (zxx): the symbol, or the value with its unit (the fine-structure constant and the proton-electron mass ratio are dimensionless and have none). Notes: on value cards, whether the value is exact or rounded and why (BIPM Table 1 and its statement that the defining constants have no uncertainty; arXiv Table XXXIII's "exact" with "..." for the derived constants; arXiv p. 62: the 2019 SI "made important physicochemical constants such as the molar gas constant R, Faraday constant F, and Stefan-Boltzmann constant σ exactly known"), plus a few facts that help learning, each from a content source: the years since which c, Δν_Cs and Kcd have had fixed values, 1983, 1967 and 1979 (BIPM Appendix 1: Resolution 1 of the 24th CGPM, 2011, PDF pp. 76 and 78, and the abrogation list in Resolution 1 of the 26th CGPM, 2018, PDF p. 85), μ₀ before 2019 (BIPM Section 2.3.1), α⁻¹ ≈ 137.04 (arXiv Table XXXIII, inverse fine-structure constant 137.035 999 177), 1 u = m(¹²C)/12 (arXiv Table XXXIII and its footnotes), λₘₐₓ = b/T (arXiv Table XXXIII: "Wien displacement law constants b = λmaxT"), kB as another symbol for k (BIPM Appendix 1), CODATA's unit J Hz⁻¹ for h (arXiv Table XXXIII), ħ read "h-bar" / "h-streck" (Wikidata aliases of Q2115969). On symbol cards, notes only where a subscript cannot be written in Unicode, for ħ, and for k (also written kB).

Cross-checks. Every value was checked against NIST's listing (all 35) and, for the 28 non-defining constants, against the published article's Table XXXIII; every defining constant against both BIPM and STAFS. The builder's Wikidata checks confirm, for each constant, the item's NIST/CODATA ID (P1645), its English (and, where Wikidata's wording is the card's, Swedish) label or alias, and its numerical value (P1181) where Wikidata holds the CODATA 2022 or exact value. Where Wikidata disagrees with CODATA 2022 the check was left out and the discrepancy recorded (Quality control, round 0).

The dossier was assembled by a script (make_dossier.py, under Queries) from a hand-written file with the metadata and documentation, the card table in the script (names, symbols, units, notes and the Swedish evidence quotes, typed from the pages as fetched) and the downloaded sources: the arXiv, APS and NIST evidence of each card quotes the line of the source's text layer that holds the value's digits, and the Wikidata evidence quotes the labels, IDs and values returned by the SPARQL query q3.

Review rounds 1-6 (Quality control) corrected notes (R and F terminate; TP also contains k; c, Δν_Cs and Kcd have had fixed values since 1983, 1967 and 1979, not 2019; the four Planck-unit notes say the value is measured, through G; the Wien note says b gives λₘₐₓ), added notes and evidence (R∞, kB, λₘₐₓ; BIPM evidence for the three years), fixed a Swedish Wikipedia locator, restored NE's pronunciation brackets in two quotes, corrected the attribution of the BIPM evidence to the 24th CGPM (2011) resolution, documented the Selection reasoning (Hartree energy, c₁ and c₂, the overlap with Swedish Wikipedia's table) inlined the helper scripts under Queries and corrected the Faraday constant's digit count in Selection and Method (18 significant digits, not 19). The fixes were applied by editing this dossier directly (round 5 with fix_round5.py, round 6 with fix_round6.py, both under Queries); make_dossier.py was not rerun.
selection: 35 constants, two cards each: (a) the seven defining constants of the SI (caesium hyperfine frequency, speed of light in vacuum, Planck constant, elementary charge, Boltzmann constant, Avogadro constant, luminous efficacy Kcd); (b) seven constants that have been exact since 2019 as combinations of the defining constants and are written rounded (five of them have endless decimals; R and F terminate, but after 15 and 18 significant digits): reduced Planck constant, molar gas constant, Faraday constant, Stefan-Boltzmann constant, Wien wavelength displacement law constant, first and second radiation constants; (c) 21 measured constants: Newtonian constant of gravitation, vacuum magnetic permeability, vacuum electric permittivity, characteristic impedance of vacuum, fine-structure constant, Rydberg constant, Bohr radius, electron Compton wavelength, classical electron radius, electron, proton and neutron mass, atomic mass constant, proton-electron mass ratio, Bohr magneton, nuclear magneton, electron magnetic moment, and the Planck length, mass, time and temperature. Left out: the Josephson constant, von Klitzing constant, magnetic flux quantum and conductance quantum, because no Swedish source confirming a Swedish name was found (Swedish Wikipedia full-text search for "flödeskvantum", "Josephsonkonstanten" and "von Klitzings konstant" returned no hits, and NE has no article under the names tried); the Hartree energy, for scope: it is the atomic unit of energy (Swedish Wikipedia's article Hartree treats it as "en enhet för energi på atomnivå"), and units are left out (see below). An earlier version of this text gave a missing Swedish name as the reason; that was wrong, since Swedish Wikipedia's table in Fysikalisk konstant names it "Hartree-energi" (a red link). The Swedish names of the first and second radiation constants (c₁, c₂) rest on the same kind of evidence: one row each in that table, red links without an article (MediaWiki API, 2026-10-04), so they are the weakest-attested Swedish names in the deck; they were kept because they are the companions of σ and b in the radiation laws; the standard acceleration of gravity (9.806 65 m s⁻²) and the standard atmosphere (101 325 Pa), which CODATA lists as adopted conventional values, not fundamental constants; the electron volt, the unified atomic mass unit and the Hartree energy as units (the atomic mass constant mᵤ = 1 u is included); the inverse fine-structure constant as a separate card (it is in the α note); the many particle-specific constants (muon, tau, deuteron, helion, magnetic-moment ratios, g-factors) and the proton charge radius, whose value has changed notably between adjustments. The cut-off is the 2022 adjustment: the 2026 CODATA adjustment had not been published on 2026-10-04. Where the list comes from: the brief asked for about 35 well-known constants, the seven SI defining constants first; the rest were chosen from CODATA's Table XXXIII (arXiv, CC BY 4.0), which groups the constants as universal, electromagnetic, atomic and nuclear, and physicochemical: from the universal and physicochemical groups the constants that are exact since 2019, the Planck units and G; from the electromagnetic and atomic groups the constants of the electron, proton and neutron and the magnetons; then filtered by the Swedish-name rule. Overlap with Swedish Wikipedia's table: 28 of the 35 constants are also rows of the 34-row table "Lista över fysikaliska konstanter" in Fysikalisk konstant, because both are lists of the best-known CODATA constants (that table itself cites CODATA 1998). The deck has 7 constants the table lacks (ΔνCs, Kcd, b, λC, rₑ, mₚ/mₑ, TP) and leaves out 6 of its rows (Hartree energy, g-factor of the free electron, proton magnetic moment, proton gyromagnetic ratio, the shielded proton moment ratio and the shielded proton gyromagnetic ratio); its order, grouping, names, symbols and values are not the table's. The table was read only to confirm Swedish names (see Licensing).

"""Read the NIST CODATA 2022 ASCII table, pick the deck's constants and round them to 5 significant figures.
Usage: python3 values.py  (prints one line per constant; writes values.json)"""
import json, re
from decimal import Decimal, ROUND_HALF_EVEN

D = "<scratch>/"
NAMES = [
    "hyperfine transition frequency of Cs-133", "speed of light in vacuum", "Planck constant", "elementary charge",
    "Boltzmann constant", "Avogadro constant", "luminous efficacy", "reduced Planck constant", "molar gas constant",
    "Faraday constant", "Stefan-Boltzmann constant", "Wien wavelength displacement law constant",
    "first radiation constant", "second radiation constant", "Newtonian constant of gravitation",
    "vacuum mag. permeability", "vacuum electric permittivity", "characteristic impedance of vacuum",
    "fine-structure constant", "inverse fine-structure constant", "Rydberg constant", "Bohr radius", "Compton wavelength",
    "classical electron radius", "electron mass", "proton mass", "neutron mass", "atomic mass constant",
    "proton-electron mass ratio", "Bohr magneton", "nuclear magneton", "electron mag. mom.", "Planck length",
    "Planck mass", "Planck time", "Planck temperature",
]
rows = {}
for line in open(D + "allascii.txt", encoding="utf-8"):
    if len(line) < 60 or line.startswith(("-", " ")):
        continue
    name = line[:60].strip()
    rest = line[60:]
    value = rest[:25].strip()
    unc = rest[25:47].strip()
    unit = rest[47:].strip()
    rows[name] = (value, unc, unit)

out = {}
for n in NAMES:
    value, unc, unit = rows[n]
    exact = unc == "(exact)"
    v = value.replace(" ", "").replace("...", "")
    num = Decimal(v.replace("e", "E"))
    q = num.copy_abs()
    exp = q.adjusted()  # power of ten of the leading digit
    rounded = num.scaleb(-exp).quantize(Decimal("1.0000"), rounding=ROUND_HALF_EVEN)
    out[n] = {"value": value, "uncertainty": unc, "unit": unit, "exact": exact,
              "mantissa5": str(rounded), "exp10": exp}
    print(f"{n:45s} | {value:28s} | {unc:24s} | {unit:18s} | 5sf {rounded}e{exp}")
json.dump(out, open(D + "values.json", "w"), indent=1)

findings.resolution: Searched Swedish Wikipedia for five phrasings (0 hits each; qc1_search.py). Kept the cards and documented the name 'kvoten mellan protonens och elektronens massor' as our own descriptive translation, an explicit exception in the Selection step of Method.

findings.resolution: Verified the overlap against the saved wikitext (28 shared; 7 deck items not in the table; 6 table rows not in the deck).
